1: import type { CommanderSuggestionDTO } from '../types';
2: import { visibleThemeLabels } from './suggestions';
3: 
4: /** A facet's selection: values the user wants to require, and values they
5:  * want to rule out. A value never appears in both at once. */
6: export interface FilterSelection {
7:   include: string[];
8:   exclude: string[];
9: }
10: 
11: export type FilterMode = 'include' | 'exclude';
12: 
13: export interface SuggestionFilters {
14:   colors: FilterSelection;
15:   /**
16:    * A further, independent restriction by identity *size* rather than
17:    * membership: colorless (identity is empty) or multicolor (2+ colors).
18:    * Kept as its own facet rather than folded into `colors` — "must be a
19:    * subset of {B, G}" and "must have 2+ colors" are different kinds of
20:    * question — but its values ('colorless' | 'multicolor') use the same
21:    * include/exclude cycle as every other facet, and render as chips inside
22:    * the same "Colors" filter row.
23:    */
24:   colorCategory: FilterSelection;
25:   brackets: FilterSelection;
26:   themes: FilterSelection;
27: }
28: 
29: const EMPTY_SELECTION: FilterSelection = { include: [], exclude: [] };
30: 
31: export const EMPTY_FILTERS: SuggestionFilters = {
32:   colors: EMPTY_SELECTION,
33:   colorCategory: EMPTY_SELECTION,
34:   brackets: EMPTY_SELECTION,
35:   themes: EMPTY_SELECTION,
36: };
37: 
38: export function hasActiveFilters(filters: SuggestionFilters): boolean {
39:   return (Object.values(filters) as FilterSelection[]).some(
40:     (selection) => selection.include.length > 0 || selection.exclude.length > 0,
41:   );
42: }
43: 
44: /** Where a value currently sits in a facet: required, ruled out, or neither. */
45: export function modeOf(selection: FilterSelection, value: string): FilterMode | null {
46:   if (selection.include.includes(value)) return 'include';
47:   if (selection.exclude.includes(value)) return 'exclude';
48:   return null;
49: }
50: 
51: /** Cycles a single value through off → include → exclude → off. */
52: export function cycleSelection(selection: FilterSelection, value: string): FilterSelection {
53:   const mode = modeOf(selection, value);
54:   const include = selection.include.filter((v) => v !== value);
55:   const exclude = selection.exclude.filter((v) => v !== value);
56: 
57:   if (mode === null) return { include: [...include, value], exclude };
58:   if (mode === 'include') return { include, exclude: [...exclude, value] };
59:   return { include, exclude };
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Color filtering is "touches this color" for "include": picking Black keeps
64:  * anything whose identity intersects it — mono-black, Golgari, a five-colour
65:  * pile — rather than only things that fit entirely inside what's picked. A
66:  * colourless commander touches nothing, so it no longer survives a colour
67:  * include; the `colorless` chip in `colorCategory` is how you ask for those
68:  * instead. "Exclude" is unchanged: the literal complement, dropping any
69:  * identity that touches an excluded color at all.
70:  *
71:  * This used to be subset semantics ("picking {B, G} keeps everything
72:  * playable in a Golgari deck"), which is why mono-black could vanish from a
73:  * rainbow pool the moment you clicked Black — the pip could ask for
74:  * commanders this list has none of, with no way to ask "what's the best
75:  * black deck in this pool?" instead. See docs/recommendation-coverage.md.
76:  */
77: function matchesColors(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
78:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
79:   if (include.length > 0) {
80:     const allowed = new Set(include);
81:     if (!suggestion.colorIdentity.some((color) => allowed.has(color))) return false;
82:   }
83:   if (exclude.length > 0) {
84:     const excluded = new Set(exclude);
85:     if (suggestion.colorIdentity.some((color) => excluded.has(color))) return false;
86:   }
87:   return true;
88: }
89: 
90: /**
91:  * `colorCategory` matches on identity *size* rather than membership, so
92:  * each value is checked as its own boolean rather than set membership.
93:  * Selecting both 'colorless' and 'multicolor' as "include" is a legal but
94:  * self-defeating combination (nothing is both) — that falls out of the
95:  * same AND semantics every other include facet already uses, rather than
96:  * needing special-casing here.
97:  */
98: function matchesColorCategory(
99:   suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO,
100:   selection: FilterSelection,
101: ): boolean {
102:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
103:   if (include.length === 0 && exclude.length === 0) return true;
104:   const isColorless = suggestion.colorIdentity.length === 0;
105:   const isMulticolor = suggestion.colorIdentity.length >= 2;
106:   const satisfies = (value: string) => (value === 'colorless' ? isColorless : isMulticolor);
107:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.every(satisfies)) return false;
108:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.some(satisfies)) return false;
109:   return true;
110: }
111: 
112: /** Included themes are AND-ed (must have all); excluded themes are ruled out
113:  * if the suggestion has any of them. Matched against the same "still has
114:  * supporting cards after the identity filter" set the card display uses, so
115:  * a filter chip never claims a theme that suggestion isn't actually showing
116:  * as a reason. */
117: function matchesThemes(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
118:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
119:   if (include.length === 0 && exclude.length === 0) return true;
120:   const present = new Set(visibleThemeLabels(suggestion));
121:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.every((theme) => present.has(theme))) return false;
122:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.some((theme) => present.has(theme))) return false;
123:   return true;
124: }
125: 
126: function matchesBracket(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
127:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
128:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.includes(suggestion.bracket.range)) return false;
129:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.includes(suggestion.bracket.range)) return false;
130:   return true;
131: }
132: 
133: export function applyFilters<T extends CommanderSuggestionDTO>(
134:   suggestions: T[],
135:   filters: SuggestionFilters,
136: ): T[] {
137:   return suggestions.filter(
138:     (s) =>
139:       matchesColors(s, filters.colors) &&
140:       matchesColorCategory(s, filters.colorCategory) &&
141:       matchesBracket(s, filters.brackets) &&
142:       matchesThemes(s, filters.themes),
143:   );
144: }
145: 
146: /**
147:  * The filter values worth offering, taken from the results themselves — no
148:  * point showing a Bracket 4–5 toggle when nothing in the list is Bracket 4–5.
149:  * Themes are drawn from the same "still has supporting cards" set the card
150:  * display uses, so a filter chip never offers a theme no suggestion actually
151:  * shows.
152:  */
153: export function availableFilterValues(suggestions: CommanderSuggestionDTO[]) {
154:   const brackets = new Set<string>();
155:   const themes = new Set<string>();
156:   const colors = new Set<string>();
157:   let hasColorless = false;
158:   let hasMulticolor = false;
159: 
160:   for (const suggestion of suggestions) {
161:     brackets.add(suggestion.bracket.range);
162:     visibleThemeLabels(suggestion).forEach((theme) => themes.add(theme));
163:     suggestion.colorIdentity.forEach((color) => colors.add(color));
164:     if (suggestion.colorIdentity.length === 0) hasColorless = true;
165:     if (suggestion.colorIdentity.length >= 2) hasMulticolor = true;
166:   }
167: 
168:   return {
169:     brackets: [...brackets].sort(),
170:     themes: [...themes].sort(),
171:     colors,
172:     hasColorless,
173:     hasMulticolor,
174:   };
175: }

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first — it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root — API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` — downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded — see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /

- `pnpm run lint` in either — no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score — see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/coverage.ts`** is a second, clearly-labelled tier beneath `synergy.ts`'s
  own two bars, not a lower bar on them — see
  [`../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md`](../../docs/recommendation-coverage.md). Every commander
  already in the submitted list gets suggested regardless of whether it clears `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT`
  (reason `'owned'`), and a relaxed, narrowest-identity-first pick covers whatever card the
  confident tier still didn't cite (reason `'covers'`). `routes/recommend.ts` sends this as
  `alsoPlayable`, serialized through the same `serialize()`/`cardIndex` the confident `suggestions`
  use — never a second index.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. **Read
  [`../../docs/archetypes.md`](../../docs/archetypes.md) before changing this file** — it is the
  reviewable catalog of what those roles and archetypes are _meant_ to mean, derived from twenty real
  decks, and it records which current behaviours are deliberate (so they don't get "fixed") and which
  are known gaps. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`

  commander — see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card

  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, Partner—[text], Partner with [Name], Friends

  by threading whole card objects through a new code path.

  wrapped by `queries.ts` (TanStack Query hooks). The `retry`/`refetchOnWindowFocus`/
  `refetchOnReconnect: false` defaults in `main.tsx` are load-bearing against Commander
  Spellbook traffic — don't restore them without re-reading the api-policy doc.
- **`client/src/store/`** splits by what the state _is_: `useAppStore` (not persisted — textarea
  contents, submitted list, dismissals) vs. `usePreferencesStore` (persisted to `localStorage` —
  durable UI prefs, currently just `combosPerPage`). Don't merge these; a dismissal surviving a
  browser restart against a different pasted list would be surprising, but a durable preference
  should outlive the tab. The suggestion grid itself has no page-size preference any more — it's
  virtualized (`@tanstack/react-virtual`), not paginated, so there's no "how many per page" to
  remember.

  filters/sort are search params on the one route (`lib/searchSchema.ts`'s
  `validateRecommenderSearch`), not `useState` — shareable and survives a refresh, which neither
  Zustand store's split above was designed for. Its `basepath` reads `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` at
  runtime rather than hardcoding `/` — this app is deployed under `/recommender` as part of the
  combined platform static site (root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Combined deploy"), and `vite.config.ts`'s
  `base` is what actually sets `BASE_URL` per build.

  "Black/Green"). Mana glyph paths and cost parsing live in `@mtg/mana` (`packages/mana`), shared
  with the sibling app — this client has no `manaSymbols.ts` of its own anymore.

  this client's own `store/` — `useAuth`, `useCardPreferences`, `useComboPreferences`, all backed
  by Supabase (RLS, owner-only), plus `AccountMenu`/`AuthDialog` themselves (this client no longer
  has its own copies — it renders `@mtg/ui`'s shared `NavBar` with `@mtg/profile`'s `AccountMenu`
  in its `accountSlot`, same as apps/home and apps/time-counters). `LikeDislikeButtons.tsx`
  (`CommanderCard`'s badge row), `JankToggle` (inside `CardDetailDialog.tsx`), and
  `ComboFavoriteButton.tsx` (inside `ComboFinder.tsx`) are this client's own remaining consumers —
  the annotate-in-place UI apps/home's `/profile` page now also has a browse-and-manage view over.

  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.

  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this

12: 
13: export interface SuggestionFilters {
14:   colors: FilterSelection;
15:   /**
16:    * A further, independent restriction by identity *size* rather than
17:    * membership: colorless (identity is empty) or multicolor (2+ colors).
18:    * Kept as its own facet rather than folded into `colors` — "must be a
19:    * subset of {B, G}" and "must have 2+ colors" are different kinds of
20:    * question — but its values ('colorless' | 'multicolor') use the same
21:    * include/exclude cycle as every other facet, and render as chips inside
22:    * the same "Colors" filter row.
23:    */
24:   colorCategory: FilterSelection;
25:   brackets: FilterSelection;
26:   themes: FilterSelection;
27: }
28: 
29: const EMPTY_SELECTION: FilterSelection = { include: [], exclude: [] };
30: 
31: export const EMPTY_FILTERS: SuggestionFilters = {
32:   colors: EMPTY_SELECTION,
33:   colorCategory: EMPTY_SELECTION,
34:   brackets: EMPTY_SELECTION,
35:   themes: EMPTY_SELECTION,
36: };
37: 
38: export function hasActiveFilters(filters: SuggestionFilters): boolean {
39:   return (Object.values(filters) as FilterSelection[]).some(
40:     (selection) => selection.include.length > 0 || selection.exclude.length > 0,
41:   );
42: }
43: 
44: /** Where a value currently sits in a facet: required, ruled out, or neither. */
45: export function modeOf(selection: FilterSelection, value: string): FilterMode | null {
46:   if (selection.include.includes(value)) return 'include';
47:   if (selection.exclude.includes(value)) return 'exclude';
48:   return null;
49: }
50: 
51: /** Cycles a single value through off → include → exclude → off. */
52: export function cycleSelection(selection: FilterSelection, value: string): FilterSelection {
53:   const mode = modeOf(selection, value);
54:   const include = selection.include.filter((v) => v !== value);
55:   const exclude = selection.exclude.filter((v) => v !== value);
56: 
57:   if (mode === null) return { include: [...include, value], exclude };
58:   if (mode === 'include') return { include, exclude: [...exclude, value] };
59:   return { include, exclude };
60: }

62: /**
63:  * Color filtering is "touches this color" for "include": picking Black keeps
64:  * anything whose identity intersects it — mono-black, Golgari, a five-colour
65:  * pile — rather than only things that fit entirely inside what's picked. A
66:  * colourless commander touches nothing, so it no longer survives a colour
67:  * include; the `colorless` chip in `colorCategory` is how you ask for those
68:  * instead. "Exclude" is unchanged: the literal complement, dropping any
69:  * identity that touches an excluded color at all.
70:  *
71:  * This used to be subset semantics ("picking {B, G} keeps everything
72:  * playable in a Golgari deck"), which is why mono-black could vanish from a
73:  * rainbow pool the moment you clicked Black — the pip could ask for
74:  * commanders this list has none of, with no way to ask "what's the best
75:  * black deck in this pool?" instead. See docs/recommendation-coverage.md.
76:  */
77: function matchesColors(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
78:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
79:   if (include.length > 0) {
80:     const allowed = new Set(include);
81:     if (!suggestion.colorIdentity.some((color) => allowed.has(color))) return false;
82:   }
83:   if (exclude.length > 0) {
84:     const excluded = new Set(exclude);
85:     if (suggestion.colorIdentity.some((color) => excluded.has(color))) return false;
86:   }
87:   return true;
88: }

92:  * each value is checked as its own boolean rather than set membership.
93:  * Selecting both 'colorless' and 'multicolor' as "include" is a legal but
94:  * self-defeating combination (nothing is both) — that falls out of the
95:  * same AND semantics every other include facet already uses, rather than
96:  * needing special-casing here.
97:  */
98: function matchesColorCategory(
99:   suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO,
100:   selection: FilterSelection,
101: ): boolean {
102:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
103:   if (include.length === 0 && exclude.length === 0) return true;
104:   const isColorless = suggestion.colorIdentity.length === 0;
105:   const isMulticolor = suggestion.colorIdentity.length >= 2;
106:   const satisfies = (value: string) => (value === 'colorless' ? isColorless : isMulticolor);
107:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.every(satisfies)) return false;
108:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.some(satisfies)) return false;
109:   return true;
110: }
111: 
112: /** Included themes are AND-ed (must have all); excluded themes are ruled out
113:  * if the suggestion has any of them. Matched against the same "still has
114:  * supporting cards after the identity filter" set the card display uses, so
115:  * a filter chip never claims a theme that suggestion isn't actually showing
116:  * as a reason. */
117: function matchesThemes(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
118:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
119:   if (include.length === 0 && exclude.length === 0) return true;
120:   const present = new Set(visibleThemeLabels(suggestion));
121:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.every((theme) => present.has(theme))) return false;
122:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.some((theme) => present.has(theme))) return false;
123:   return true;
124: }
125: 
126: function matchesBracket(suggestion: CommanderSuggestionDTO, selection: FilterSelection): boolean {
127:   const { include, exclude } = selection;
128:   if (include.length > 0 && !include.includes(suggestion.bracket.range)) return false;
129:   if (exclude.length > 0 && exclude.includes(suggestion.bracket.range)) return false;
130:   return true;
131: }

133: export function applyFilters<T extends CommanderSuggestionDTO>(
134:   suggestions: T[],
135:   filters: SuggestionFilters,
136: ): T[] {
137:   return suggestions.filter(
138:     (s) =>
139:       matchesColors(s, filters.colors) &&
140:       matchesColorCategory(s, filters.colorCategory) &&
141:       matchesBracket(s, filters.brackets) &&
142:       matchesThemes(s, filters.themes),
143:   );
144: }
145: 
146: /**
147:  * The filter values worth offering, taken from the results themselves — no
148:  * point showing a Bracket 4–5 toggle when nothing in the list is Bracket 4–5.
149:  * Themes are drawn from the same "still has supporting cards" set the card
150:  * display uses, so a filter chip never offers a theme no suggestion actually
151:  * shows.
152:  */

154:   const brackets = new Set<string>();

162:     visibleThemeLabels(suggestion).forEach((theme) => themes.add(theme));

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions —
including Partner/Background pairs — with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time — the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first — it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
